# Warbler of Care Plans (`warbler-of-care-plans`)

Checks home care hours against the plan of care or authorization week by week: services delivered with no plan behind them, hours over the weekly authorization that will not be paid, weeks delivered well short of the plan, and plans or authorizations ending soon. Client names are masked before results reach the model.

**Warbler never requests plan or authorization changes. Warbler never submits or changes claims.**

Kestrel ver 1 · Home care · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · patient and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`kestrel-core`](../kestrel-core)

```bash
npx -y warbler-of-care-plans demo
npx -y warbler-of-care-plans mcp --root ./practice-files
```

## What the sample data shows

Fictional data only: a made-up home care agency and clients. Any likeness to real people is chance.

- [`plans.csv`](fixtures/plans.csv) and [`visits.csv`](fixtures/visits.csv) for the weeks of November 2 and 9, 2026. Planted:
  - Jon Pike: 14 homemaker hours in the week of November 2 against 10 authorized.
  - Kim Soto: 15 of 25 authorized hours in the week of November 9.
  - Lou Dean: 4 hours of respite (S5150) on November 5 with no plan covering it.
  - Ida Marsh: the plan ends December 1.
- [`settings.json`](fixtures/settings.json): two weeks checked, 20% short counts as under-delivery, 30-day warning, example hourly rates. [`settings-typo.json`](fixtures/settings-typo.json) misspells a setting and is refused.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `warbler_check` | List services not on the plan, over-delivery, under-delivery and plans ending. | runs |
| `warbler_write_report` | Write warbler-care-plans.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and warbler-care-plans.html into out_dir (default kestrel-out/warbler). | runs |
| `warbler_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `warbler_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `warbler_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `warbler_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `plan_change_submit` | Warbler never requests plan or authorization changes. | refused |
| `claim_submit` | Warbler never submits or changes claims. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `warbler_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `plans` (required) | Plans of care or authorizations under --root: client, service, weekly hours, start and end, authorization number |
| `visits` (required) | Delivered visits: client, date, service, hours (or minutes, or clock in and out) |
| `settings` | Optional settings JSON: weeks, under_pct, warn_days, rates |
| `as_of` | Date to measure deadlines and ages from (YYYY-MM-DD); default today |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold patient or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx warbler-of-care-plans inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### Plans of care (`plans`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | text (masked) | Client ID, Client #, Member ID, Medicaid ID, Participant ID, Patient ID |
| `client_name` | text (masked) | Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Participant, Patient Name |
| `service` | text | Service, Service Code, HCPCS, Procedure, Code, Service Type |
| `weekly_hours` | number | Weekly Hours, Hours per Week, Authorized Hours, Approved Hours, Hours/Week |
| `start` (required) | date | Start, Start Date, Effective, From, Auth Start |
| `end` | date | End, End Date, Through, Thru, Auth End, Expires |
| `auth_number` | text | Auth #, Authorization, Auth Number, Plan ID, PA # |

### Visits (`visits`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | text (masked) | Client ID, Client #, Member ID, Medicaid ID, Participant ID, Patient ID |
| `client_name` | text (masked) | Client, Client Name, Member, Member Name, Participant, Patient Name |
| `date` (required) | date | Date of Service, DOS, Service Date, Visit Date, Date, From DOS, Session Date, Appointment Date |
| `service` | text | Service, Service Code, HCPCS, Procedure, Code, Service Type |
| `hours` | number | Hours, Hours Worked, Visit Hours, Duration (hrs) |
| `minutes` | number | Minutes, Min, Mins, Duration, Duration (min), Time (min), Total Minutes, Treatment Minutes |
| `clock_in` | text | Clock In, Start Time, Time In |
| `clock_out` | text | Clock Out, End Time, Time Out |

## Settings file (`warbler_settings`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `weeks` | Full weeks to check, ending with the last full week on or before as_of; default 4 |
| `under_pct` | Percent short of authorized hours that counts as under-delivery; default 20 |
| `warn_days` | Days ahead to warn about plans ending; default 30 |
| `rates` | Hourly rate by service code, for dollar estimates |

## Memory

`warbler_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `warbler_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `kestrel-core` and `remedy-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "warbler-of-care-plans": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "warbler-of-care-plans",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/practice-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add warbler-of-care-plans -- npx -y warbler-of-care-plans mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
warbler-of-care-plans tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
warbler-of-care-plans sources               # the columns each input is read from
warbler-of-care-plans inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
warbler-of-care-plans call warbler_check '{"plans":"<plans>","visits":"<visits>"}'
warbler-of-care-plans eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
warbler-of-care-plans demo
```

## Patient and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: patient and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to an EHR, practice-management system, payer portal, clearinghouse, state system, HR or payroll system, or bank.
- Payer, Medicare, Medicaid, state and federal rules are summarised from public material as of 2026, and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, compliance or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, billing, coding, tax, clinical or HIPAA advice. It does not diagnose or recommend care. A person decides what to bill, pay, report, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
